svg.text: 剑影 JIÀNYǏNG · COLOUR AND ENCHANTMENT — PROPOSAL
The figures are the game's own geometry. The colour and the auras are NOT in the game — this sheet is the proposal.
Rarity lives in the bleed, not the body
Every stroke is drawn twice: a wide faint bleed, then solid ink. Tinting the BLEED reads as the piece glowing out of the paper; tinting the body would
just make a coloured cut-out and throw the silhouette away.
Flat ink. Most of what drops.
A gold hairline along the piece.
Cinnabar, and the ink bleeds wider.
The bleed becomes a wash of qi.
An inscription is one thing you can see standing still
Each rite has a single effect that reads in a still frame. An enchantment only visible in motion cannot be compared in the hub, which is where a
player decides whether the drop was worth anything.
A cold wash clings to the
The progression sheet showed the five schools converging on one black mass at the end of the road — the endgame armour dominates and the weapon is a
thin line. Same five figures here, each carrying a different rite.
The budget, which matters more than the palette
Auras belong to the player and to drops on the ground — never to the swarm. Two hundred glowing enemies would cost the frame budget AND destroy
the readability the silhouettes were chosen for. One rite lit at a time, and two added pigments in total: 靛 indigo and 石绿 malachite.
